When you want to understand metrics such as "visits", "average interaction depth", "usage time", "stay time", "bounce rate", "exit rate", etc., you need to introduce a session to analyze, and the custom session analysis in BytePlus Growth Analysis quickly supports session\-related analysis. This article shows you how to create a custom session and use custom session analysis.

<span id="_1-概述"></span>
# **Background information**

The following introduces the basic general concepts of the session, and the detailed calculation principle can be seen [Session](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Session_).

**What is a session?** 

Session is a conversation, a series of interactions that users include in a single visit that occurs on your website/H5/Mini Program /APP. For example, a conversation is a visit, and a visit can include any one of multiple web pages or screen views, events, social interactions, and e\-commerce transactions, and can include some or all of them.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

**Session cutting time**

The session cut time is the longest acceptable time interval between two events when they are triggered. If the time interval between the two actions exceeds the cutting time, the session is cut. It can also be understood that when the user performs an action and does not perform a follow\-up action after the cutting time, the access session is considered to have ended. After that, other behaviors are started, which is regarded as the start of another new session. On the basis of the transaction table, the generated session_id correlates the single point behavior events of the same user, and finally forms a session composed of a sequence of events.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

For example, in the picture, user A starts to open the App at 10:52 am, first searches, 2 minutes later, starts to browse the activity page, 6 minutes later, searches again, it is already 11 am, get off work time, and colleagues go out for lunch for 1h, go back to the previous search results page, start browsing the product details page, and find that it is not what you want, so change a few keywords, repeat the search, and finally find the product you want, browse the product details page again, and feel very like it, collect the product, the end of the visit.

Suppose we set the cutting time to 30 minutes, user A has two sessions, and user A has no follow\-up behavior for 30 minutes after the second search, so the first session ends at 11:30 am. When the user starts accessing again at 12 o'clock, the second session has already started.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">The session cutting time is not the maximum (long) time range of the session, so be sure to distinguish it.</div>


<span id="_2-快速入门"></span>
# Operation process

Growth Analytics provides you with the ability to customize sessions. After creating a custom session, you can choose to switch session analysis in the event analysis tool. The main operating process is as follows.


1. Create a custom session in the **custom session** interface of **data management**, and define the events to be analyzed in this custom session, the segmentation strategy of the session, etc.

2. Enter the **event analysis** page, switch to session analysis, configure parameters such as analysis indicators, and view the analysis query result data.


See below for detailed operation steps.

<span id="_3-功能介绍"></span>
# Operation steps

<span id="777a7d52"></span>
## New Custom Session


1. After logging into the Growth Analytics console, click **Data Management** \> **Metadata Management** \> **Custom Session** in the top navigation bar to enter the Custom Session page.

2. Click the **New Session** button in the upper right corner to configure the new session parameters in the pop\-up page, including **basic information**, **included events** and **cutting methods**.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/bf6b2af4d34741b9aac638c604c758fc~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

3. Configure **basic information**.

   In the basic information, the session name must be entered, and the display name can be selected. The session name is not allowed to be repeated. If there is a duplicate name, the system will give an error prompt ("Session name is not allowed to be repeated") when finally saving, and saving is not allowed.

4. Configure **the included events**.

   In the drop\-down list of the selection box, select the event that needs to be added to the custom session, and subsequent added events can be used as indicators in the event analysis.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">tip   </div>
   

   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="1">The system defaults to the <strong>session as a whole</strong>, <strong>any event</strong> (any_event), so you don't need to manually add any event to the custom session.   </div>
   

   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="1">It supports adding up to 100 events to the Session. If the "Add" button is grayed out, the number of events may reach 100.   </div>
   

5. Configure the **cutting method**.

   You need to configure the time for session cutting first, and then choose whether you want to configure event cutting and inter\-session cutting as needed.

   
   |**Parameter** |**Configuration instructions** |**Configuration suggestion** |
   |---|---|---|
   |**Time cutting** |* Cutting rule: Determine whether a session needs to be cut by the interval between any two of the included events. If the time interval exceeds the set time cut, the two events are divided into two sessions before and after.<br><br>* Configuration instructions: Select the duration of time cutting in the interface, and the granularity includes:<br><br>   * Seconds: up to 3600<br><br>   * Minutes: up to 1440<br><br>   * Hours: up to 24<br><br>   * Default: granularity is divided into points, value is blank |Usually 30 minutes is recommended for the web, and 1 to 2 minutes is recommended for Apps and Mini Programs. If there are special scenarios, such as video playback and online educational courses, delay adjustments can be made. |
   |**Event cutting** |* Cutting rule: Determines whether to force the start/end of a session by specifying the start/end event of the session.<br><br>* Configuration instructions: Select the start event and end event in the interface.<br><br>   * You can configure only the start event or only the end event.<br><br>   * Both the start event and the end event must be the selected event in "Included Events"; and the start and end events cannot be the same.<br><br>   * Only one start/end event can be configured. |The following scenarios suggest configuring event cutting:<br><br><br>* For example, short video apps need to calculate the number of concurrent viewers watching live broadcasts simultaneously.<br><br>* The tool app needs to calculate the number of concurrent video conferences. At this point, it is not necessary to calculate the overall number of online users of the app, but to calculate the number of concurrent users of a certain type of function. When creating a session, it is necessary to exclude other events and only calculate and analyze the events related to the scene. |
   |**Cross\-time cutting** |* Cutting rule: The switch configuration for cutting across time periods is applicable to whether to cut the session if the session crosses the time granularity range of the query analysis when the event analysis tool is used for session query analysis later.<br><br>   For example, the time granularity of the session query for event analysis is days. When the start time of a session is 23:50 the day before and the end time is 00:10 the day after, you need to use this switch to determine whether the session needs to be cut.<br><br>   * Check Cross\-time cutting: then the session needs to be cut, and the session will appear in the query data results of both the previous and the next day.<br><br>   * Do not check Cross\-time cutting: the session will not be cut, and the session will only appear in the previous day's query data results.<br><br>* Configuration instructions: Check whether to turn on the inter\-period cutting switch as needed in the interface.<br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Due to the complexity of the calculation, the downloaded data may be different from the data in the chart.</div><br> |Does not involve |

# FAQ

<span id="02867fda"></span>
## **Q1: How to set the session cutting time rule?** 

Answer: Usually 30 minutes is recommended for the web, and 1 to 2 minutes is recommended for Apps and Mini Programs. If there are special scenarios, such as video playback and online education courses, delay adjustment can be made.

<span id="9bec4c9a"></span>
## **Q2: When does the session choose event cutting?** 

Answer: For example, short video apps need to calculate the number of concurrent viewers watching live broadcasts at the same time; tool apps need to calculate the number of concurrent video conferencing concurrently. At this point, it is not necessary to calculate the overall number of online users of the app, but to calculate the number of concurrent users of a certain type of function. When creating a session, it is necessary to exclude other events and only calculate and analyze the events related to the scene.

<span id="08632737"></span>
## **Q3: The final result and the expected experience value feel that the gap is relatively large, what should I do if it is not accurate?** 

Answer: The calculation of the session itself is an approximation. The final result is closely related to the rules of the cutting time and the selection of events. You can try to change different cutting rules.

<span id="8ef42db8"></span>
## **Q4: The overall usage duration of the session, what is the difference between the duration of a certain event?** 

Answer: The duration of the session as a whole refers to the duration of all events added when the session was created. Selecting a single event depends on the duration of only one event.
